*(Session note, J267: the seat wrote this closing round at the head of `checks/M0-e-04.md`; the session moved it, unchanged, into this file — the session-round convention (`M0-e-04-s1.md`) — and recorded it as `check-M0-e-04-s2`; the first-check file and its record `check-M0-e-04` stand as committed.)*

Lane `check/M0-e-04-close-s2` ran under Opus 5.5 in Claude Code in a cloud container (Linux x64, Node 24.12.0).
`tools/machine_profile.py --id` printed `linux:Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.80GHz:4cpu:16gib`. The seat ran on
2026-10-11 from about 06:22 to 08:50 (UTC). It is an implementer-side, independent checker, not the item's author
(`build/M0-e-04`, `-fix1`, `-int-g13-fix1`, `-fix-s1` and `-fix-s2`: L-0269, L-0285, L-0304, L-0326 and L-0405). It
closes the session fix round S2 opened on ruling N-56 (2) (J249). It is not the re-check of a failed check.

The seat ran no git command. It changed no file of the item. It planned its probes and mutants before it read the
author's self-check. It ran one vitest process at a time (`tools/test_budget.py` printed 1 worker and `--mutants` 1
throughout). Its mirrors are `m1` (a tar copy of `plat/` without `node_modules`, the tree as landed) and `m2` (the
same, used for the identity mutant and the sweep), under the session scratchpad's `waves/check-M0-e-04/`. Each was
installed with `corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline` (exit 0). No symbolic link in either resolves into
the tree, and `@plat/kernel` resolves inside the mirror. The vitest config resolves `@plat/*` through the
`plat-source` condition to `src/`, so a mutant of `src/` reaches testkit's tests too. The pre-round behaviour is
reproduced exactly by the identity mutant (`mergeCollinear` returns `ring.slice()`): the round's only code change is
the merge and its two call sites, and the merge returns an equal copy when a ring has no exactly collinear vertex. The
checker's ledger row is **L-0409**.

## Verdict: PASS. N-56 (2) Q21 (collinear) is fixed and no new blocker was found

| line | re-run (this seat) | verdict | label |
|---|---|---|---|
| **N-56 (2) Q21 (collinear)**: a lawful simple ring with collinear vertices is refused by `settlementPerimeter`'s `isSumRing` after the union merges them | **The code.** `perimeter.ts` adds `mergeCollinear(ring)`: it drops a vertex v when `orient2d(a, v, b) === 0` and `(v − a) · (b − v) > 0`, in one pass against the original neighbours. It keeps a fold back (dot < 0) and a repeat (dot = 0), and returns a copy when nothing is dropped. `settlementPerimeter` computes `const b = mergeCollinear(boundary)` before the convolution, the two fast rings and the overlay. `isSumRing` begins with `const boundary = mergeCollinear(given)`. `index.ts` exports `mergeCollinear`. **The ruling's evidence, re-run with this seat's own probes.** On SMALL_FLAT seed 1165799859, S5's last outline (31 points, 0 collinear) was given M0-x-06's `collinear` kind (42 points, `simpleCcw` true). S6 then runs with no refusal and commits the clean run's perimeter: 310 points, sha256 prefix `6455a8e440db8202`, 16 districts, `unowned` 0, and the whole S6 output identical to the clean run's. With the pre-round code (m2, identity), the same run is refused: `E_INVARIANT settlementPerimeter: the overlay's outer ring is not the boundary's offset (the sum check failed)`. Next, a 300 m square was tested with its four side midpoints, under all 8 rotations of the start, and with 10 drawn splits of 1 to 6 interior lattice points per side (7 to 18 points). All of these give the clean square's perimeter (`2779fe698c5d0c34`). With the identity mutant, every split gives a different ring. **The ruling's invariance, more widely.** This seat's own property: 300 random star rings on a 1 m lattice (5 to 24 vertices, about 30 % of them with deep notches, a 400 m frame clip on every third). Each ring was split at drawn lattice points and compared with the clean ring started at the same vertex: **300/300 byte-identical** with the fix. 81 of the calls took the overlay path (a counter instrumented in the mirror). With the identity mutant, 296 of 300 differ and 2 are refused `E_INVARIANT`. **Zero shift.** The 100 count-law towns (`town(1..100)`) carry 0 exactly collinear vertices. With the fix and with the identity mutant, the digest of their 100 perimeters is `0617ad24549920ecf0c361dc8c6dfaff60e3daffcc0428e89f4cd84ee7dad2f6` (equal to the value `collinear.test.ts` pins), and this seat's digest of the whole `runS6` output over the 100 (`29590d77…`) is identical. A SMALL_FLAT census over seeds 401–480, a range outside the author's 1–400, reached S6 on 80 of 80, with 0 outlines carrying a collinear vertex and 0 S6 refusals. Every per-seed S6 result was identical with the fix and with the identity mutant (census digest `20c435f3…` in both). **The shift, by rule.** Seed 103's natural outline (116 points, 1 collinear vertex) gives a perimeter of 313 points with the fix and 314 with the pre-round code. This seat merged that outline with the probe's own exact merge (independent of the library) and ran the pre-round code on it: the result is the fix's output (`8e2fb0fd…`, S6 `e270e4ac…`). The shift is therefore exactly the merge. **The pins stand.** In m1, `collinear.test.ts` and `collinear-chain.test.ts` give `Tests 7 passed (7)`. With the identity mutant they give `Tests 7 failed (7)`. | **fixed** | CONFIRMED |

**The self-touching and coincident cells.** The ruling read both refusals as lawful and their pins as staying. The
coincident ring on 2708765650 is still refused `E_INVARIANT settlementPerimeter: the union: insert: no route from
(-20142, 2587) to (-20177, 2577) keeps clearance (§3.10) within the fidelity bound (N-43)`, with nothing committed and
the same refusal with the pre-round code. That pin stays. The self-touching ring on 2191303060 is now absorbed. C-0305
(4) calls its refusal the same collinear defect, and this seat confirms that by causality. The natural outline (104
points) carries 2 exactly collinear vertices. With the pre-round code, the self-touching kind on that outline is
refused `E_INVARIANT … (the sum check failed)`. The same kind laid on the outline after the probe's own merge (102
points, then 105) commits under the pre-round code. Its S6 output (perimeter 332 points `af5a1002…`, 11 districts,
`unowned` 0, a simple perimeter, sum-checked against the given ring) is byte-identical to the fix's output on the
unmerged ring. The refusal was therefore the Q21 defect, not a lawful refusal. The absorbed outcome is EP-01's
preferred outcome for that cell, and in M0-x-06's own table it is the majority outcome (absorbed 995). Changing the
round's pin from refused to absorbed is a correction backed by evidence, not a deviation. CONFIRMED. *Session note:*
M0-x-06's round 2 re-pins `EP-01/S6/self-touching` on 2191303060 as absorbed (C-0305 (4)). Its table records that cell
as "not pinned", so no committed test turns red.

| K02 `isSumRing` without its own merge | "`isSumRing` merges the boundary it is given" (C-0305 (2)) | killed (2 failed) |

| K05 repeats merged (dot ≥ 0) | "a repeated vertex … is kept" | killed (1) |

| K07 the first vertex never merged | the wrap at index 0 | killed (1) |
| K08 the last vertex never merged | the wrap at n − 1 | killed (3) |
| K09 the left neighbour read from the output (sequential) | "one pass against the original neighbours, order-free" | **survives: equivalent**. 200 000 random small rings with runs, spikes, repeats and zero-area cases all give identical output, because a dropped neighbour lies on the same line, behind v. |
| K10 the ring itself returned when nothing merges | "comes back as a copy" | killed (1) |
| K11 the overlay's union fed the unmerged boundary | C-0305 (2)'s "the overlay" | **survives: equivalent**. The kernel's union merges the collinear vertices itself (the round's own cause).
